I read the full spec and all six evidence paths. Verdict below.

## Bottom line

The preregistration cannot deliver its own bounded claim. It will reliably detect that the installed 16-channel composite is a strict contraction with a unique fixed point — but that outcome is close to guaranteed by construction (two orthogonal-axis dephasers plus non-commuting Lindblad dissipation compose to a generic strict contraction on the Bloch ball). The one test that carries the "distinctive rather than generic" burden (T9) is underspecified and underpowered, and the correct null for that question — the same channels in permuted order — is preregistered as unscored (T8). So the experiment can earn "REAL" trivially and cannot legitimately earn "DISTINCTIVE".

## Fatal defects

**F1 — T9 cannot carry "distinctive".** "Matched random primitive CPTP cycles" leaves the null distribution unregistered: matched on what (Kraus count, dissipation budget, collapse-operator norms, rotation angles)? Contractio
